answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, persistent stake rather than account count: an agent must lock tokens for each vote or job bid, and slashing removes that stake when fraud is proven. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply voting power; it divides the same capital and adds setup and monitoring costs. An umber ledger can record deposits, while a haven for appeals checks evidence; the fable of effortless, free identities ends when every false persona risks real funds.
